criteria.criterion: With the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 attached, the firmware changes the STSPIN830 drive-enable signal between enabled and disabled states.
criteria.observable: STSPIN830 drive-enable GPIO level while firmware is commanded to enable and disable drive
preconditions: X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 is connected to the NUCLEO-G431RB.
The firmware is running on the NUCLEO-G431RB.
The driver enable input is accessible for measurement.
procedure: Power the connected NUCLEO-G431RB and X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1.
Command the firmware to enable drive and measure the driver-enable GPIO.
Command the firmware to disable drive and measure the driver-enable GPIO.
criteria.expected: The driver-enable signal is in the enabled state after the enable command and in the disabled state after the disable command.

criteria.criterion: With the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 attached, the firmware produces PWM on the driver input associated with TIM1.
criteria.observable: PWM waveform at the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 driver input
preconditions: X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 is connected to the NUCLEO-G431RB.
The firmware is running and drive is enabled.
A suitable oscilloscope or logic analyzer is connected to the driver input.
procedure: Enable motor drive in the firmware.
Probe the configured TIM1 PWM output at the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 input.
Record the observed waveform while the firmware is commanded to produce drive.
criteria.expected: A periodic PWM waveform is present at the configured driver input while drive is enabled.

criteria.criterion: When commanded to start with the GBM2804H-100T connected and powered, the motor exhibits observable rotation.
criteria.observable: Mechanical movement or rotation of the GBM2804H-100T rotor
preconditions: The motor is correctly connected to the U, V, and W outputs.
The motor driver is powered.
The firmware is running on the NUCLEO-G431RB.
procedure: Issue the firmware's motor-start command.
Observe the GBM2804H-100T rotor during the commanded run interval.
Record whether the rotor moves or rotates.
criteria.expected: The rotor exhibits observable movement or rotation after the start command.

criteria.criterion: The firmware's motor pole-pair configuration used by motor calculations or reporting is set to 7.
criteria.observable: Motor pole-pair configuration constant or configuration value in the source/configuration and its compiled use
preconditions: The firmware source and build configuration are available for inspection.
procedure: Locate the motor pole-pair configuration used by the firmware.
Verify its configured value and any generated or compiled configuration that supplies it.
criteria.expected: The configured motor pole-pair value is exactly 7 pairs.

criteria.criterion: The motor-driver supply measured at the test setup is 12 V DC.
criteria.observable: Bench-supply output voltage measured with a voltmeter at the motor-driver supply input
preconditions: A bench supply is available.
The motor driver is connected to the bench supply.
procedure: Set the bench supply for the test.
Measure the DC voltage at the motor-driver supply input with a voltmeter before or during the motor test.
Record the measured voltage and polarity.
criteria.expected: The measured supply is 12 V DC.

criteria.criterion: The three motor phase connections use the hardware output terminals labeled U, V, and W.
criteria.observable: Physical wiring from the motor phases to the driver-board U, V, and W terminals
preconditions: The motor is connected to the motor-driver board.
procedure: Inspect the motor-driver output terminal labels.
Trace each motor phase connection to its terminal.
Record the terminal labels used.
criteria.expected: The three motor phase connections terminate at U, V, and W, with no motor phase connected to another output.

criteria.criterion: A clean firmware build completes for the NUCLEO-G431RB without compiler, linker, or build errors.
criteria.observable: Build command exit status, build log, and generated firmware image
preconditions: The required toolchain is installed.
The project is configured for the NUCLEO-G431RB target.
procedure: Run the documented clean-build command.
Inspect the build exit status and log.
Confirm that the firmware image is generated.
criteria.expected: The clean build exits successfully with no build errors and produces a firmware image for the NUCLEO-G431RB.

criteria.criterion: The generated firmware image flashes to the NUCLEO-G431RB and the board executes it without changing the image or source after the build.
criteria.observable: Programmer output and target-board startup/run indication after flashing
preconditions: A clean firmware image has been built.
A programmer and NUCLEO-G431RB are available and powered.
No source or firmware-image changes are made after the clean build.
procedure: Flash the generated firmware image to the NUCLEO-G431RB using the programmer.
Inspect the programmer result.
Power-cycle or reset the board and observe its startup/run indication or other firmware-defined execution indication.
criteria.expected: Programming completes successfully, the flashed image is unchanged from the clean-build artifact, and the NUCLEO-G431RB powers up and executes that image without source or binary modification.

criteria.criterion: With the firmware initialized, TIM1 produces three simultaneous PWM signals on the U, V, and W driver-input connections with a common synchronized time base.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope traces on the STSPIN830 U, V, and W inputs
preconditions: Board is powered.
Firmware is initialized.
The U, V, and W signals are connected to the corresponding STSPIN830 inputs.
procedure: Power the NUCLEO-G431RB and connected driver board.
Initialize the firmware.
Probe the U, V, and W inputs with a three-channel oscilloscope.
Compare the carrier timing and presence of PWM on all three channels.
criteria.expected: Three active PWM waveforms are present simultaneously on U, V, and W, and their carrier timing is synchronized.

criteria.criterion: The driver configuration selects the factory three-PWM-input mode and contains no configuration that selects an alternate commutation mode.
criteria.observable: Driver-mode configuration code, GPIO configuration, and project configuration
preconditions: Driver board is at factory defaults.
The firmware source and configuration are available for review.
procedure: Inspect the STSPIN830 mode-selection configuration.
Verify that the three PWM inputs are assigned to the driver interface.
Search the configuration and initialization code for alternate commutation-mode selection.
criteria.expected: The factory three-PWM-input mode is selected, and no alternate commutation mode is configured.

criteria.criterion: When PWM is enabled without an active fault, the U, V, and W PWM duty cycles form three sinusoidal modulation signals separated by 120 electrical degrees.
criteria.observable: Time-aligned oscilloscope traces or captured duty-cycle envelope for U, V, and W
preconditions: PWM is enabled.
No active driver or firmware fault is present.
A commanded electrical frequency is set.
procedure: Enable PWM with no active fault.
Capture the U, V, and W driver-input waveforms over multiple electrical cycles.
Determine the phase of each channel's sinusoidal duty-cycle envelope relative to the others.
criteria.expected: The three modulation envelopes are phase-shifted by 120 electrical degrees, within the measurement resolution.

criteria.criterion: The phase sequence of the three PWM modulation envelopes advances at the commanded electrical frequency.
criteria.observable: Measured period or frequency of the repeating U-V-W modulation sequence
preconditions: PWM is enabled.
No active driver or firmware fault is present.
A commanded electrical frequency is known.
procedure: Set a known commanded electrical frequency.
Capture the U, V, and W driver-input waveforms.
Measure the repetition frequency of the phase sequence.
criteria.expected: The measured electrical frequency equals the commanded electrical frequency within the measurement resolution.

criteria.criterion: Driving STBY to its standby level places the STSPIN830 in standby, and driving it to its enable level places the driver in the enabled state.
criteria.observable: STBY GPIO level and STSPIN830 driver state or output-enable behavior
preconditions: The board and driver are powered.
The firmware exposes or executes STBY control.
The STSPIN830 datasheet-defined STBY polarity is used.
procedure: Command STBY to the standby level and observe the driver state or disabled outputs.
Command STBY to the enable level and observe the driver state or enabled outputs.
Record the STBY level and corresponding driver state after each command.
criteria.expected: The standby-level command results in the datasheet-defined standby/disabled state, and the enable-level command results in the datasheet-defined enabled state.

criteria.criterion: The measured TIM1 PWM carrier frequency is 20 kHz.
criteria.observable: PWM carrier period or frequency on a TIM1 output
preconditions: PWM is enabled.
An oscilloscope or frequency counter is connected to a TIM1 PWM output.
procedure: Enable PWM.
Measure the carrier frequency over multiple PWM periods.
Compare the measurement with 20 kHz.
criteria.expected: The carrier frequency is 20 kHz within the measurement resolution.

criteria.criterion: At entry to the startup ramp, the commanded PWM duty-cycle amplitude is 10%.
criteria.observable: Startup-ramp amplitude command or TIM1 compare values at ramp entry
preconditions: The firmware is initialized.
The startup ramp is about to begin.
The PWM timer state or amplitude command is observable.
procedure: Trigger the startup ramp.
Capture the first amplitude command or corresponding TIM1 compare value at ramp entry.
Convert the compare value to duty-cycle percentage using the configured PWM period.
criteria.expected: The initial commanded PWM amplitude is 10%.

criteria.criterion: The effective PWM duty cycle on every output remains at or below 20% when a duty command greater than 20% is applied.
criteria.observable: Measured high-time duty cycle on the TIM1 U, V, and W outputs
preconditions: PWM is enabled.
A duty command greater than 20% can be issued.
The three PWM outputs are accessible to a measurement instrument.
procedure: Enable PWM.
Issue a duty command greater than 20%.
Measure the effective duty cycle on U, V, and W.
Repeat for any output whose command can be independently varied.
criteria.expected: No measured output duty cycle exceeds 20%.

criteria.criterion: At entry to the startup ramp, the generated electrical frequency is 1 Hz.
criteria.observable: Measured period or frequency of the three-phase modulation sequence at ramp entry
preconditions: The startup ramp is about to begin.
PWM generation is active or begins with the ramp.
The U, V, and W waveforms are measurable.
procedure: Trigger the startup ramp.
Capture the phase sequence beginning at ramp entry.
Measure its electrical frequency.
criteria.expected: The initial electrical frequency is 1 Hz within the measurement resolution.

criteria.criterion: During the startup ramp, the generated electrical frequency reaches 10 Hz and does not exceed 10 Hz without an explicit reconfiguration command.
criteria.observable: Time history of the measured electrical frequency and the command/reconfiguration log
preconditions: The startup ramp is in progress or its target is set.
No explicit frequency reconfiguration command is issued during the limiting portion of the test.
The three-phase waveforms are measurable.
procedure: Start the startup ramp with a target of 10 Hz.
Measure the electrical frequency throughout the ramp and after it reaches its target.
Verify that no explicit frequency reconfiguration command was issued.
Check the maximum measured frequency and whether 10 Hz was reached.
criteria.expected: The measured frequency reaches 10 Hz, never exceeds 10 Hz while unreconfigured, and remains at the target until explicitly reconfigured.

criteria.criterion: After issuing DIR CW and then DIR CCW, the measured phase order changes to match the most recently commanded direction.
criteria.observable: U-V-W phase order before and after each direction command
preconditions: The motor is rotating or about to start.
PWM is enabled or will be enabled by the start command.
The direction commands can be sent over UART.
procedure: Issue `DIR CW` and capture the U, V, and W phase sequence.
Issue `DIR CCW` and capture the phase sequence again.
Compare each measured phase order with the corresponding last direction command.
criteria.expected: The phase order after `DIR CW` matches the CW sequence, and the phase order after `DIR CCW` is the reversed CCW sequence and remains the sequence associated with the last command.

criteria.criterion: The motor's observed rotation direction reverses when the command changes from DIR CW to DIR CCW.
criteria.observable: Motor shaft rotation direction before and after the direction command
preconditions: The motor is connected to the driver.
PWM is enabled and the motor is rotating or about to start.
The motor and driver are operated within the permitted test conditions.
procedure: Issue `DIR CW` and observe the motor shaft direction.
Issue `DIR CCW` and observe the motor shaft direction after the command takes effect.
Compare the two observed directions.
criteria.expected: The motor rotates in the CW direction after `DIR CW` and in the opposite, CCW direction after `DIR CCW`.

criteria.criterion: At the first sample of the startup ramp, the commanded PWM duty is 10%.
criteria.observable: TIM1 commanded duty cycle at startup-ramp entry
preconditions: Startup ramp has just begun
PWM/GPIO initialization has succeeded
No active STSPIN830 fault
procedure: Initialize the motor-control hardware.
Issue MOTOR START.
Capture the first PWM duty command produced by the startup-ramp handler.
criteria.expected: 10% duty at startup-ramp entry

criteria.criterion: Every PWM duty command generated during the startup ramp is no greater than the configured maximum amplitude.
criteria.observable: PWM duty values emitted by the startup-ramp control function
preconditions: Startup-ramp function is exercised with a configured initial amplitude of 10%
A maximum amplitude is configured
procedure: Call the portable startup-ramp function through successive time steps.
Record each generated PWM duty command.
Compare each value with the configured maximum amplitude.
criteria.expected: Each duty value is less than or equal to the configured maximum amplitude
criteria.rationale: This check is derived from the postcondition requiring the amplitude not to exceed the maximum limit; the limit is already a configuration parameter rather than an invented numeric threshold.

criteria.criterion: The measured electrical frequency samples collected during startup are monotonically non-decreasing from the configured initial frequency toward the 10 Hz ramp target.
criteria.observable: Measured electrical frequency over the startup-ramp interval
preconditions: Startup ramp is in progress
Frequency measurement is connected to the motor-control output
procedure: Start the motor and record electrical-frequency samples throughout the startup ramp.
Verify that each sample is greater than or equal to the preceding sample.
Verify that the samples begin at the configured initial frequency and approach the configured target.
criteria.expected: Frequency never decreases and reaches the configured 10 Hz target

criteria.criterion: With ADC measurement, motor-parameter, characterization, FOC, observer, current-sensing, and closed-loop-control features disabled or absent, a MOTOR START command produces the first startup-ramp PWM command.
criteria.observable: UART response and TIM1 PWM output after MOTOR START
preconditions: PWM/GPIO initialization has succeeded
No active STSPIN830 fault
All listed out-of-scope features are disabled or absent
UART is operational
procedure: Boot the firmware with the listed features disabled or absent.
Send MOTOR START over UART.
Observe the startup-ramp state or first PWM output.
criteria.expected: Startup-ramp state is entered and PWM startup output begins

criteria.criterion: When PWM/GPIO initialization succeeds and EN/FAULT is inactive, MOTOR START is accepted and the startup ramp begins.
criteria.observable: UART command result and startup-ramp state/PWM output
preconditions: System is booted
PWM/GPIO initialization has reported success
STSPIN830 EN/FAULT is inactive
procedure: Apply the successful initialization result and inactive EN/FAULT input.
Send MOTOR START over UART.
Observe the command result and motor-control state.
criteria.expected: MOTOR START is accepted and the state changes to startup ramp

criteria.criterion: When PWM/GPIO initialization fails or EN/FAULT is active, MOTOR START does not enable PWM or enter the startup ramp.
criteria.observable: TIM1 PWM outputs and motor-control state after MOTOR START
preconditions: System is booted
At least one start prerequisite is false: PWM/GPIO initialization failure or active EN/FAULT
procedure: Set the selected prerequisite to its failing condition.
Send MOTOR START over UART.
Observe the PWM outputs and motor-control state.
criteria.expected: PWM remains disabled and the startup-ramp state is not entered

criteria.criterion: After reset or power-up, STBY remains at the configured disable level until TIM1/GPIO configuration is complete and PWM outputs are at their defined inactive levels.
criteria.observable: STSPIN830 STBY level, TIM1/GPIO configuration-complete event, and three PWM input pins
preconditions: The NUCLEO-G431RB is cold-booted or reset
Oscilloscope or logic analyzer is connected to STBY and all three driver inputs
procedure: Reset or power-cycle the board.
Record STBY and the three driver-input pins during initialization.
Correlate the first transition of STBY to the TIM1/GPIO configuration-complete event.
criteria.expected: STBY remains at the configured disable level until configuration completion, and all three PWM inputs are at their defined inactive levels before STBY is enabled

criteria.criterion: After STBY is enabled, the motor remains stopped until a valid MOTOR START command is received.
criteria.observable: Driver-input waveforms and motor shaft motion before and after command
preconditions: Initialization has completed
STBY is enabled
No UART command has yet been issued
procedure: Observe the driver inputs and motor before issuing a command.
Send a valid MOTOR START command.
Continue observing the inputs and motor.
criteria.expected: No motor drive or motion occurs before MOTOR START; startup PWM begins only after the valid command

criteria.criterion: After MOTOR STOP or while EN/FAULT is active, all three driver-input pins remain at the documented inactive levels and show no PWM switching.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope traces of the three STSPIN830 input pins and EN/FAULT
preconditions: PWM is enabled or the startup ramp is in progress
The factory three-input STSPIN830 configuration and documented inactive levels are known
procedure: Capture the three driver-input pins while PWM is active.
Issue MOTOR STOP, then repeat with EN/FAULT asserted.
Measure the pin levels and switching activity after each event.
criteria.expected: All three inputs are continuously at their documented inactive levels with no switching after either event

criteria.criterion: Following MOTOR STOP, STATUS reports Stopped and following an EN/FAULT event, STATUS reports the applicable fault state.
criteria.observable: UART STATUS response
preconditions: The motor was enabled or in startup ramp
UART is operational
procedure: Issue MOTOR STOP and request STATUS.
Assert EN/FAULT and request STATUS.
Compare each response with the corresponding event.
criteria.expected: MOTOR STOP produces STATUS=Stopped, and an asserted EN/FAULT produces STATUS indicating the active driver fault

criteria.criterion: When the inactive driver-input level cannot be driven, STBY is asserted to the configured disable level.
criteria.observable: STBY level during an injected inactive-level drive failure
preconditions: PWM disable is requested
A test fault prevents at least one driver input from reaching its configured inactive level
procedure: Inject the driver-output failure.
Issue MOTOR STOP or assert EN/FAULT.
Observe STBY and the driver-input pins.
criteria.expected: STBY is at the configured disable level and the driver is forced into standby
criteria.rationale: This check is derived from the stated failure behavior; it verifies the specified safety fallback when the primary inactive-level action cannot be completed.

criteria.criterion: Immediately after initialization and before any command, the three driver-input pins show no PWM activity and the motor remains stopped.
criteria.observable: Driver-input waveforms and motor motion before the first command
preconditions: The board has just completed reset/initialization
No UART or other motor command has been issued
procedure: Complete reset and initialization.
Observe all three driver-input pins and the motor before sending any command.
criteria.expected: No PWM transitions are present and the motor does not move

criteria.criterion: A UART MOTOR START command begins the open-loop startup ramp with the configured initial amplitude and configured initial frequency.
criteria.observable: UART command handling result, initial PWM duty, and initial electrical-frequency command
preconditions: UART is operational
PWM/GPIO initialization has succeeded
No active STSPIN830 fault
procedure: Send the exact UART command MOTOR START.
Capture the first amplitude and frequency commands produced by the startup sequence.
Compare them with the configured initial values.
criteria.expected: The startup-ramp state begins; first amplitude equals the configured initial amplitude and first frequency equals the configured initial frequency

criteria.criterion: While PWM is enabled or the startup ramp is active, receiving MOTOR STOP disables all PWM outputs within one control cycle.
criteria.observable: Timestamped UART MOTOR STOP reception and PWM output transition
preconditions: PWM is enabled or startup ramp is in progress
The motor is being driven
A control-cycle period is measurable
procedure: Start the motor or wait until the ramp is active.
Send MOTOR STOP and timestamp command reception.
Measure the interval until all three PWM outputs reach their disabled/inactive state.
criteria.expected: All PWM outputs are disabled no later than one control cycle after MOTOR STOP reception

criteria.criterion: After MOTOR STOP, the motor is no longer driven.
criteria.observable: Motor phase drive waveform and motor motion after stop
preconditions: The motor is enabled or in startup ramp
MOTOR STOP has been received
procedure: Issue MOTOR STOP.
Observe the phase-drive waveforms and motor motion after the PWM-disable transition.
criteria.expected: No phase-drive waveform remains and the motor is not driven

criteria.criterion: When EN/FAULT is asserted while PWM is enabled, all PWM outputs are disabled within one control cycle.
criteria.observable: Timestamped EN/FAULT transition and PWM output transition
preconditions: PWM is currently enabled
A control-cycle period is measurable
The STSPIN830 EN/FAULT signal can be asserted
procedure: Run the motor with PWM enabled.
Assert EN/FAULT and timestamp the transition.
Measure the interval until all three PWM outputs reach their disabled/inactive state.
criteria.expected: All PWM outputs are disabled no later than one control cycle after EN/FAULT assertion

criteria.criterion: PWM remains disabled after an EN/FAULT event until the fault clears and a new MOTOR START command is received.
criteria.observable: PWM output state across fault assertion, fault clearing, and subsequent command
preconditions: PWM is enabled
EN/FAULT can be asserted and cleared
UART is operational
procedure: Assert EN/FAULT and verify PWM is disabled.
Clear EN/FAULT without issuing a command and observe PWM.
Issue MOTOR START and observe PWM again.
criteria.expected: PWM remains disabled after fault clearing alone and resumes only after the subsequent MOTOR START command
criteria.rationale: This check is derived from the requirement's failure behavior, which explicitly requires the disabled state to persist until both fault clearance and a re-commanded start occur.

criteria.criterion: After transmitting `DIR CW`, the observed motor phase sequence is clockwise and the reported direction is CW.
criteria.observable: Motor phase outputs and direction field in STATUS
preconditions: System is initialized
UART is operational
Motor drive and phase outputs are connected
procedure: Transmit the command `DIR CW` using the configured UART settings.
Capture the generated phase sequence over at least one electrical cycle.
Request `STATUS` and record the direction field.
criteria.expected: The phase sequence corresponds to clockwise rotation and STATUS reports `CW`.

criteria.criterion: After transmitting `DIR CCW`, the observed motor phase sequence is counter-clockwise and the reported direction is CCW.
criteria.observable: Motor phase outputs and direction field in STATUS
preconditions: System is initialized
UART is operational
Motor drive and phase outputs are connected
procedure: Transmit the command `DIR CCW` using the configured UART settings.
Capture the generated phase sequence over at least one electrical cycle.
Request `STATUS` and record the direction field.
criteria.expected: The phase sequence corresponds to counter-clockwise rotation and STATUS reports `CCW`.

criteria.criterion: After transmitting `FREQ x`, the measured electrical frequency is x Hz by the next control update.
criteria.observable: Measured electrical frequency from the phase/PWM output
preconditions: PWM is enabled or ready to enable
UART is operational
A frequency value x is selected
procedure: Transmit `FREQ x`.
Observe the phase or timer output after the next control update.
Measure its electrical frequency.
criteria.expected: Measured electrical frequency equals x Hz within the test instrument's stated measurement tolerance by the next control update.

criteria.criterion: The effective PWM duty after a `DUTY x` command equals x percent for x at or below 20 and is no greater than 20 percent for x above 20.
criteria.observable: TIM1 PWM output duty cycle
preconditions: PWM is enabled or ready to enable
UART is operational
procedure: Transmit `DUTY 10` and measure the effective PWM duty.
Transmit `DUTY 25` and measure the effective PWM duty.
criteria.expected: The first measurement is 10% within the measurement tolerance; the second measurement is less than or equal to 20%.

criteria.criterion: A `STATUS` response contains a field whose value unambiguously identifies the current motor state.
criteria.observable: STATUS UART response motor-state field
preconditions: STATUS is requested
UART is operational
procedure: Put the motor in a known state.
Transmit `STATUS`.
Parse the response fields.
criteria.expected: The response contains a motor-state field with an unambiguous state value such as `Stopped`, `Running`, or `Ramping`.

criteria.criterion: A `STATUS` response contains a direction field whose value is either CW or CCW and matches the configured direction.
criteria.observable: STATUS UART response direction field
preconditions: STATUS is requested
UART is operational
The direction has been set to a known value
procedure: Set the direction to CW or CCW.
Transmit `STATUS`.
Parse the direction field.
criteria.expected: The response contains `CW` or `CCW` matching the configured direction.

criteria.criterion: A `STATUS` response contains a numeric electrical-frequency field in Hz matching the internal frequency setpoint or measurement.
criteria.observable: STATUS UART response frequency field
preconditions: STATUS is requested
UART is operational
A known electrical frequency is configured
procedure: Set a known frequency.
Transmit `STATUS`.
Parse the numeric frequency field and compare it with the internal setpoint or measured frequency.
criteria.expected: The response contains a numeric Hz value equal to the current internal setpoint or measurement within the defined measurement tolerance.

criteria.criterion: A `STATUS` response contains a numeric PWM-duty field in percent matching the effective duty within measurement tolerance.
criteria.observable: STATUS UART response duty field and measured PWM duty
preconditions: STATUS is requested
UART is operational
PWM is active
procedure: Set a known duty value within the safe limit.
Measure the effective PWM duty.
Transmit `STATUS`.
Parse the numeric duty field.
criteria.expected: The reported percentage matches the measured effective PWM duty within the test's stated measurement tolerance.

criteria.criterion: A `STATUS` response contains a driver-fault field that reflects whether the STSPIN830 EN/FAULT condition is active.
criteria.observable: STATUS UART response fault field and injected/read driver fault condition
preconditions: STATUS is requested
UART is operational
The driver fault input can be observed or controlled
procedure: Run `STATUS` with the driver fault inactive and record the fault field.
Activate or inject the driver fault condition.
Run `STATUS` again.
criteria.expected: The fault field indicates inactive in the first case and active in the second case.

criteria.criterion: Transmitting `DIR CW` and then `DIR CCW` updates the internal direction state to CW and then CCW, with each value appearing in the subsequent STATUS response.
criteria.observable: Direction field in two successive STATUS responses
preconditions: UART is operational
System is initialized
procedure: Transmit `DIR CW` and request `STATUS`.
Transmit `DIR CCW` and request `STATUS`.
Compare the direction fields with the commands.
criteria.expected: The first STATUS reports `CW` and the second STATUS reports `CCW`.

criteria.criterion: The firmware configuration and interface documentation each specify the UART port, baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, and command delimiter, and the values agree.
criteria.observable: UART configuration source/configuration and interface documentation
preconditions: Firmware source/configuration and the interface documentation are available
procedure: Inspect the UART initialization configuration.
Inspect the documented command-interface settings.
Compare all six settings.
criteria.expected: All six settings are explicitly specified in both places and are identical.
criteria.rationale: The requirement requires a fixed, specified configuration, while the stated runtime acceptance criterion alone does not establish that every required setting is documented or fixed.

criteria.criterion: Using the documented UART settings, a host transmitting `STATUS` receives a correctly formatted response containing the STATUS fields.
criteria.observable: UART response bytes received by the host
preconditions: Target is powered and running the firmware
The host uses the documented UART settings
procedure: Connect the host using the documented port and serial settings.
Transmit `STATUS` followed by the documented delimiter.
Capture and parse the response.
criteria.expected: A complete, correctly formatted STATUS response is received using the configured UART connection.

criteria.criterion: A command sent with deliberately incorrect UART settings does not produce a valid command action or a partial motor/configuration change.
criteria.observable: Pre/post STATUS values after a command sent with incorrect serial settings
preconditions: Target is powered and initialized
A known baseline STATUS is available
The host can transmit using at least one incorrect UART setting
procedure: Record STATUS before the negative test.
Transmit a state-changing command using an incorrect UART configuration.
Request STATUS using the documented configuration.
criteria.expected: No valid action is acknowledged and every motor/configuration field in STATUS remains equal to its baseline value.
criteria.rationale: This checks the stated failure behavior by observing both command recognition and state preservation after communication with mismatched settings.

criteria.criterion: An unrecognized command such as `FOO` produces an explicit error response and leaves all motor and configuration fields unchanged.
criteria.observable: UART error response and before/after STATUS responses
preconditions: UART link is established
System is initialized
procedure: Request STATUS and save all reported motor/configuration fields.
Transmit `FOO`.
Capture the response.
Request STATUS again.
criteria.expected: The command response explicitly identifies an error, and every compared STATUS field is identical before and after `FOO`.

criteria.criterion: Each invalid command `FREQ abc` and `FREQ -1` produces an error response and leaves the reported electrical-frequency value unchanged.
criteria.observable: UART error responses and before/after STATUS frequency field
preconditions: System is initialized
UART is operational
A known frequency setpoint is active
procedure: Request STATUS and record the frequency.
Transmit `FREQ abc` and capture the response.
Request STATUS and compare the frequency.
Transmit `FREQ -1` and capture the response.
Request STATUS and compare the frequency again.
criteria.expected: Both commands produce explicit error responses, and the frequency remains equal to the initial value after each command.

criteria.criterion: A `FREQ` command with a missing argument produces an error response and does not alter the electrical-frequency setpoint.
criteria.observable: UART error response and before/after STATUS frequency field
preconditions: System is initialized
UART is operational
A known frequency setpoint is active
procedure: Record the frequency from STATUS.
Transmit `FREQ` with the documented command delimiter and no argument.
Capture the response and request STATUS.
criteria.expected: The response is an explicit error and the reported frequency equals the pre-command value.
criteria.rationale: The requirement explicitly includes missing arguments, but its stated acceptance examples cover only non-numeric and negative values; this adds the missing-argument assertion.
